data.description:
## Problem
In the rebar-mcp container the tracker is `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` (the shared `gerrit_mcp_tickets` volume), so `StorePaths(tracker).rebar_dir` is `/var/gerrit/site/.rebar`, which is on each container's writable layer (confirmed read-only over SSM on 2026-11-04: not mounted, absent 11 minutes after start). `exemplary-silty-tuatara` moved the compaction lock and stamp off it. Other store-wide sidecars still live there:
- `hlc.state` / `hlc.lock` (src/rebar/_store/hlc.py): the store clock's cache and its read-modify-write lock. It is reset on each deploy, and the blue and green containers each hold their own lock over one store during the overlap.
- the recent-creates journal and its lock (src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py): reset on each deploy, and not shared across the overlap.

Unverified: whether either causes an observable defect. The HLC takes `max(state, witness, physical_now) + 1`, so a reset may be harmless; the recent-creates journal's consumers and their tolerance for a reset have not been read.

## Approach
Read each consumer and decide, per sidecar, whether a per-container reset or a split lock matters. Where it does, key it on the store, following `exemplary-silty-tuatara` (the tracker's git dir) or `intangible-ladyish-vicuna`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For each of `hlc.state`/`hlc.lock` and the recent-creates journal, the ticket records whether a per-container reset or split lock affects behaviour, with evidence.
- [ ] Every sidecar found to matter is store-scoped and shared by both MCP containers, with a regression test where 2 processes over one store have different `.rebar` dirs.
data.title: MCP .rebar sidecars beyond compaction reset per deploy
